topic: Someone finds their grandmother's engagement ring in a pawn shop
text: The light through the dusty window caught the ring, a glimmer of something familiar. I turned it in my fingers, the metal cool, the gemstone catching the sunlight. It felt right, heavy with a past I could sense but not quite grasp. The shop was quiet, the hum of the old neon sign above the door the only noise. My mind drifted, painting scenes of laughter and warmth, of stories shared over this very piece of jewelry. It called to me, and I knew, without a word, what I had to do. Slowly, I placed it down, stepping back, the decision made. Some things are meant to pass through us, leaving their mark but not their weight.
